subject: Proposed evaluation plan & success criteria for Aurora AI trial
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@auroraai.com>, Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed next steps for Aurora AI trial

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and a proposed next step so we keep momentum: 

What we agreed on during the call:
- Primary use case: semantic search + answer generation for internal knowledge base (support articles + engineering docs).
- Key constraint: data residency within US only; audit logging required.
- Success signals: 1) 20% reduction in time-to-resolution (measured on sample incidents), 2) >85% relevance on top-3 reranked results in our eval set, 3) acceptable latency under 300ms p95 for interactive queries.

Proposed next step: a 4–6 week POC focused on validating relevance and latency with a scoped dataset. I attached a short outline (Aurora_POC_outline.pdf) that proposes: timelines, owners, test dataset size, and a minimal security checklist.

Asks for you: could you confirm the primary stakeholders (who will own success criteria and procurement), and whether Aurora can provide a 50–100 doc sample export for the first week of tests? Once we have that, we can lock the kickoff date.

I copied Marissa (solutions engineering) who will run the evaluation with us. If that plan looks good I’ll send a more detailed evaluation template and schedule a 30-minute kickoff.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Hi Markus — thanks, and appreciated the clear summary. A few clarifications before we schedule: 

1) Success metrics: the ones you listed look reasonable. Can you propose how you’ll measure “time-to-resolution” during the POC (what windows, what tooling)? Also want to include a qualitative stakeholder satisfaction question at the end.
2) Data access: our security team prefers S3 pulls with encrypted transit and a short-lived service account. Is that compatible with Redwood Private or Dedicated options for the POC?
3) Timeline: Aurora’s procurement cycle sometimes takes 10–14 business days. I’m looping in procurement (procurement@auroraai.com) now so they can flag required paperwork.

We’ll aim to provide a 50-doc sample by next Wednesday. Also looping in Samir who will own technical acceptance criteria.

Thanks,

Hi Elena — great questions, answers below and an updated concrete plan attached.

1) Measuring time-to-resolution: for the POC we recommend a two-week simulated incident run: we’ll seed ~40 incidents from historical tickets and measure time from query->candidate answer->final human validation. Metric collected via a shared Google Sheet and our evaluation template; the baseline will be Aurora’s historical average over the same ticket set.

2) Data access & infra: both Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private support S3 pulls with IAM short-lived credentials and TLS. For the POC we typically spin up a temporary Dedicated pool (isolated tenant) to avoid any cross-tenant caching; we can switch to Private if Aurora prefers a customer-managed control plane. Marissa will coordinate the secure transfer and security checklist.

3) Timeline & owners (proposed):
- Week 0 (prep, approvals): procurement & security signoff — owners: Elena + procurement@auroraai.com
- Week 1 (data ingest & baseline): Marissa (SE) + Aurora data owner (TBD)
- Weeks 2–3 (relevance testing & tuning): Marissa + Markus
- Week 4 (latency/load test + final report): Marissa + Markus + Samir

If that looks good I attached the evaluation template (redwood-eval-template.xlsx) and a short set of sample prompts we recommend for relevance testing (sample-eval-prompts.txt). Please confirm: who is Aurora’s designated data owner (name and email) so we can provision S3 access with the correct ACLs.

Next steps: once you confirm stakeholder names and approve the outline I’ll send a calendar invite for a kickoff on either Tue May 26 or Thu May 28.

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eval-template.xlsx, sample-eval-prompts.txt

Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed next steps for Aurora AI trial

Hi all — jumping in from SE to add operational details and a recommended minimal test plan: 

- Test dataset: aim for 50–150 documents covering docs, FAQs, and 10 representative ticket summaries. For relevance, we’ll run a 600-query evaluation set (derived from sampled user searches + paraphrases).
- Security checklist highlights: encrypted at rest (SSE-S3), TLS 1.2+, VPC egress rules, audit log retention 90 days. We can provide SOC2 evidence and a short network diagram.
- Test harness: we’ll provide a small repo with scripts to run relevance scoring and latency collection; results will be pushed to a shared Drive folder.

Action items I can own from Redwood: prepare the evaluation harness, coordinate S3 access, run the initial baseline import. I’m available for a 30-minute kickoff demo; Markus please include the calendar invite when ready.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
